WHAT IT IS: claude-mem v15.9.0, homepage claude-mem.ai, a commercial operator (CMEM, Inc. / cmem.ai). It is a persistent-memory plugin for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Qoder, Grok, OpenClaw, Hermes, OMP, OpenCode, Windsurf, Kimi, Devin and others (installers in src/services/integrations/*). Hooks record every tool use as an "observation". A background worker (Bun, localhost:37777) compresses observations with an LLM via the Claude Agent SDK or other providers (OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Gemini, NVIDIA, xf-yun). The worker stores data in SQLite with FTS5 search, and optionally in a Chroma vector DB via uv/Python for hybrid search. Context is injected back at SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse(Read/Bash/Grep/Glob) through the "file-context" read gate. An MCP server "mcp-search" provides memory search. A server-beta stack exists (Postgres + Valkey/BullMQ, docker-compose.yml).

AGENT-INTEGRATION RISK SURFACE (for the OAW decision):
(1) plugin/hooks/hooks.json registers 9 hook events: Setup, SessionStart x3, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse(*), PostToolUseFailure(*), PreToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop and SessionEnd. PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure fire on every tool call. Most entries call a global `claude-mem` binary. Setup runs a long /bin/sh one-liner that changes PATH (nvm, ~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew) and executes version-check.js found in the plugin cache.
(2) plugin/.mcp.json starts MCP through `node -e` with an inline loader. The loader searches the plugin root, cwd/plugin, cwd, ~/.codex/plugins/cache and ~/.claude/plugins/cache, then require()s the first scripts/mcp-server.cjs it finds. Because cwd is on that path, a malicious repo opened by the agent could plant plugin/scripts/mcp-server.cjs and have it run, unless CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is set and matches first.
(3) The shipped runtime is prebuilt, minified bundles committed to git. Examples: plugin/scripts/worker-service.cjs 4.5 MB, server-service.cjs 2.3 MB, mcp-server.cjs 0.9 MB, transcript-watcher.cjs, plus a viewer bundle of about 1 MB. None of these can be reviewed or reproduced from this checkout without a build.
(4) Telemetry is ON BY DEFAULT and goes to PostHog (us.i.posthog.com). A hardcoded public key is in src/services/telemetry/common.ts. The consent order is DO_NOT_TRACK, then the CLAUDE_MEM_TELEMETRY env var, then telemetry.json, then default ON (src/services/telemetry/telemetry.ts:543).
(5) Some paths send data to the cloud. The cowork plugin streams tool use to cmem.ai. claude-mem-cursor/mcp.json defines a remote MCP at https://cmem.ai/api/mcp with a bearer token, and its Cursor hooks run `npx -y claude-mem ...` on every prompt and shell call. There is also sync.cmem.ai cloud sync.
(6) Install paths. install/public/install.sh and installer.js are now just stubs that point to `npx claude-mem install`. openclaw/install.sh (1,651 lines) pipes https://bun.sh/install and https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh into a shell, and git-clones and npm-installs. openclaw/SKILL.md tells users to run `curl https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash`. docker/claude-mem/Dockerfile also pipes bun.sh into bash and runs a global npm install of @anthropic-ai/claude-code.
(7) package.json and plugin/package.json allow native postinstall scripts (tree-sitter-*, esbuild, better-sqlite3 and others). @huggingface/transformers (local embedder, onnxruntime) is optional. .npmrc sets legacy-peer-deps=true.
(8) There are 41 SKILL.md files in total. plugin/ has 30, several of which are large automation skills: build-and-release, release, version-bump, babysit, oh-my-issues, learn-codebase ("read every source file in full"), and screenpipe (screen/audio history). The agent-cost-report skill ships 39 Python scripts with CHECKSUMS.txt. Seven git symlinks were checked out as plain text files.

RELEVANCE TO THE USER'S REQUEST (could it replace the LLM wiki?): this is an event-sourced session-memory system (hook capture, then LLM compression into SQLite FTS5 + Chroma vectors, then context injection). It is not a curated knowledge map. Its design ideas (the observation schema, the 3-step mem-search skill, the PreToolUse file-context read gate, tree-sitter "smart-explore", the timeline/knowledge-agent skills) are worth reading as patterns. The full stack is too invasive to adopt as-is: global hooks on every tool call, a default-on telemetry daemon, unreviewable prebuilt bundles, and cloud upsell paths. The safest way to adopt it would be a clean-room re-implementation of selected patterns. No instructions found in the candidate's files were acted on.
